civilopediaText.text: Experienced officers who can hit targets at extreme range.

civilopediaText.text: Firing while being dragged back by ropes - the 9th Massachusetts Battery retired 'by prolonge' from the Peach Orchard on July 2.

name: George G. Meade
uniques: [+20]% Strength bonus for [{Military} {Land}] units within [3] tiles <when defending>

civilopediaText.text: Commanding the Army of the Potomac since June 28. Fought a skillful defensive battle on interior lines, shifting brigades to each threatened point. Inspires all troops within 3 tiles when defending.

name: John F. Reynolds
uniques: [+25]% Strength bonus for [{Military} {Land}] units within [1] tiles
[+1] Movement

civilopediaText.text: Commander of the I Corps and the army's left wing; widely thought the best general in the army. He rushed his men into Herbst Woods on the morning of July 1 and was shot dead at its edge.

name: Winfield S. Hancock
uniques: [+25]% Strength bonus for [{Military} {Land}] units within [2] tiles

civilopediaText.text: 'Hancock the Superb', II Corps. Sent ahead by Meade on July 1, he rallied the broken corps on Cemetery Hill; on July 2 he plugged every gap in the line; on July 3 he was wounded repelling Pickett's Charge.

name: Oliver O. Howard
uniques: [+20]% Strength bonus for [{Military} {Land}] units within [2] tiles <when defending>

civilopediaText.text: XI Corps. Posted his reserve on Cemetery Hill at midday on July 1 - the decision that gave the army its anchor. Congress later thanked him for selecting the position.

name: Abner Doubleday
uniques: [+15]% Strength bonus for [{Military} {Land}] units within [2] tiles
[+10]% Strength <when defending>

civilopediaText.text: Commanded the I Corps after Reynolds fell and held McPherson's and Seminary Ridges for most of July 1.

name: Daniel E. Sickles
uniques: [+20]% Strength bonus for [{Military} {Land}] units within [2] tiles <when attacking>

civilopediaText.text: III Corps. A political general who, without orders, advanced his corps to the Peach Orchard salient on July 2. His leg was shattered by a cannonball at the Trostle farm.

name: Henry W. Slocum
uniques: [+20]% Strength bonus for [{Military} {Land}] units within [2] tiles <when defending>

civilopediaText.text: XII Corps, which fought for Culp's Hill on the nights of July 2 and the morning of July 3.

name: George Sykes
uniques: [+15]% Strength bonus for [{Military} {Land}] units within [2] tiles

civilopediaText.text: V Corps, the army's reserve, including the U.S. Regulars, which saved Little Round Top and fought in the Wheatfield.

name: John Sedgwick
uniques: [+15]% Strength bonus for [{Military} {Land}] units within [2] tiles
[+1] Movement

civilopediaText.text: VI Corps, the largest in the army, which marched about 34 miles to reach the field on July 2.

name: John Gibbon
uniques: [+20]% Strength bonus for [{Military} {Land}] units within [2] tiles <when defending>

civilopediaText.text: Commanded the II Corps division at the Angle that met Pickett's Charge.

name: John Buford
uniques: [+25]% Strength bonus for [Cavalry] units within [2] tiles
[+2] Sight

civilopediaText.text: Cavalry division commander with an eye for ground. He recognized the importance of the heights at Gettysburg and held off Heth's infantry on July 1 until the I Corps arrived.

name: Gouverneur K. Warren
uniques: [+2] Sight
Can see over obstacles
[+15]% Strength bonus for [{Military} {Land}] units within [2] tiles

civilopediaText.text: Meade's chief engineer. From the signal station on Little Round Top he saw Hood's division about to sweep the undefended hill and diverted troops to it just in time.

name: Henry J. Hunt
uniques: [+25]% Strength bonus for [Artillery] units within [3] tiles

civilopediaText.text: Chief of artillery of the Army of the Potomac and the best artillerist of the war. He husbanded his ammunition during the July 3 cannonade so the guns could smash Pickett's Charge.

name: David M. Gregg
uniques: [+20]% Strength bonus for [Cavalry] units within [2] tiles <when defending>

civilopediaText.text: 2nd Cavalry Division, which with Custer's brigade stopped Stuart at East Cavalry Field on July 3.

name: Judson Kilpatrick
uniques: [+20]% Strength bonus for [Cavalry] units within [2] tiles <when attacking>

civilopediaText.text: 'Kill-Cavalry'. On July 3 he ordered Farnsworth's hopeless mounted charge against Confederate infantry south of Big Round Top.

name: Robert E. Lee
uniques: [+15]% Strength bonus for [{Military} {Land}] units within [3] tiles <when attacking>

civilopediaText.text: Commanding the Army of Northern Virginia. Confident after Chancellorsville, he attacked on all three days. Inspires all troops within 3 tiles when attacking.

name: James Longstreet
uniques: [+25]% Strength bonus for [{Military} {Land}] units within [2] tiles <when defending>

civilopediaText.text: 'Old Pete', I Corps. Lee's 'old war horse' urged a move around the Union left onto defensive ground, and opposed the July 3 assault. His July 2 attack nevertheless came close to rolling up the Union line.

name: Richard S. Ewell
uniques: [+15]% Strength bonus for [{Military} {Land}] units within [2] tiles

civilopediaText.text: II Corps, Stonewall Jackson's successor. Told to take Cemetery Hill on July 1 'if practicable', he decided it was not.

name: A. P. Hill
uniques: [+15]% Strength bonus for [{Military} {Land}] units within [2] tiles

civilopediaText.text: III Corps, which opened the battle on July 1. Hill was ill during much of the battle.

name: Henry Heth
uniques: [+15]% Strength bonus for [{Military} {Land}] units within [2] tiles

civilopediaText.text: His division marched toward Gettysburg on July 1, reportedly in search of shoes, and ran into Buford's cavalry. Wounded in the head that afternoon - a wad of paper in his hat saved his life.

name: William D. Pender
uniques: [+15]% Strength bonus for [Infantry] units within [2] tiles <when attacking>

civilopediaText.text: Division commander whose brigades broke the last Union line on Seminary Ridge on July 1. Mortally wounded on July 2.

name: Robert E. Rodes
uniques: [+15]% Strength bonus for [{Military} {Land}] units within [2] tiles
[+1] Sight

civilopediaText.text: Division commander who arrived on Oak Hill on July 1 and attacked the flank of the Union I Corps.

name: Jubal A. Early
uniques: [+15]% Strength bonus for [{Military} {Land}] units within [2] tiles <when attacking>

civilopediaText.text: His division arrived from the north-east on July 1 and crushed the Union XI Corps at Barlow's Knoll.

name: Edward Johnson
uniques: [+15]% Strength bonus for [{Military} {Land}] units within [2] tiles

civilopediaText.text: 'Allegheny' Johnson, whose division assaulted Culp's Hill on the night of July 2 and again on July 3.

name: Richard H. Anderson
uniques: [+15]% Strength bonus for [{Military} {Land}] units within [2] tiles

civilopediaText.text: Division commander whose brigades struck the Union center on July 2 and briefly reached Cemetery Ridge.

name: Lafayette McLaws
uniques: [+15]% Strength bonus for [{Military} {Land}] units within [2] tiles

civilopediaText.text: Division commander whose brigades - Kershaw, Barksdale, Semmes, Wofford - overran the Peach Orchard and the Wheatfield on July 2.

name: John B. Hood
uniques: [+20]% Strength bonus for [Infantry] units within [2] tiles <when attacking>

civilopediaText.text: Commander of the division that attacked Devil's Den and Little Round Top on July 2. A shell fragment crippled his arm early in the assault.

name: George E. Pickett
uniques: [+15]% Strength bonus for [Infantry] units within [2] tiles <when attacking>

civilopediaText.text: His fresh Virginia division led the grand assault on the Union center on July 3. 'General Lee, I have no division,' he is said to have answered afterward.

name: J. E. B. Stuart
uniques: [+25]% Strength bonus for [Cavalry] units within [2] tiles
[+1] Movement
[+1] Sight

civilopediaText.text: Lee's flamboyant cavalry chief. His long raid around the Union army meant he reached Gettysburg only on the evening of July 2.

name: E. Porter Alexander
uniques: [+25]% Strength bonus for [Artillery] units within [3] tiles

civilopediaText.text: Colonel commanding Longstreet's artillery; he directed the great bombardment of July 3, the largest of the war.
